question: What are the most influential papers on Alzheimer amyloid beta? Return 5 with DOIs and citation counts.
final_text: {"answer":"The five most-cited papers on Alzheimer's amyloid beta, ranked by citation count, cover foundational topics including ApoE4 genetics, synaptic toxicity of Aβ dimers, immunotherapy, GWAS risk loci, and transgenic mouse models. (1) Strittmatter et al. (1993) established the link between ApoE4 and amyloid beta binding in late-onset Alzheimer's disease (4,220 citations). (2) Shankar et al. (2008) showed that Aβ dimers isolated from human Alzheimer's brains directly impair synaptic plasticity and memory (3,460 citations). (3) Schenk et al. (1999) demonstrated that immunization with Aβ attenuates Alzheimer-like pathology in the PDAPP mouse model (3,135 citations). (4) Kunkle et al. (2019) performed a large genetic meta-analysis implicating Aβ, tau, immunity, and lipid processing in Alzheimer's risk (2,622 citations). (5) Games et al. (1995) reported Alzheimer-type neuropathology in transgenic mice overexpressing the V717F β-amyloid precursor protein (2,519 citations).","citations":[{"doi":"10.1073/pnas.90.5.1977","title":"Apolipoprotein E: high-avidity binding to beta-amyloid and increased frequency of type 4 allele in late-onset familial Alzheimer disease.","citation_count":4220},{"doi":"10.1038/nm1782","title":"Amyloid-β protein dimers isolated directly from Alzheimer's brains impair synaptic plasticity and memory","citation_count":3460},{"doi":"10.1038/22124","title":"Immunization with amyloid-β attenuates Alzheimer-disease-like pathology in the PDAPP mouse","citation_count":3135},{"doi":"10.1038/s41588-019-0358-2","title":"Genetic meta-analysis of diagnosed Alzheimer's disease identifies new risk loci and implicates Aβ, tau, immunity and lipid processing","citation_count":2622},{"doi":"10.1038/373523a0","title":"Alzheimer-type neuropathology in transgenic mice overexpressing V717F β-amyloid precursor protein","citation_count":2519}]}

parsed.answer: The five most-cited papers on Alzheimer's amyloid beta, ranked by citation count, cover foundational topics including ApoE4 genetics, synaptic toxicity of Aβ dimers, immunotherapy, GWAS risk loci, and transgenic mouse models. (1) Strittmatter et al. (1993) established the link between ApoE4 and amyloid beta binding in late-onset Alzheimer's disease (4,220 citations). (2) Shankar et al. (2008) showed that Aβ dimers isolated from human Alzheimer's brains directly impair synaptic plasticity and memory (3,460 citations). (3) Schenk et al. (1999) demonstrated that immunization with Aβ attenuates Alzheimer-like pathology in the PDAPP mouse model (3,135 citations). (4) Kunkle et al. (2019) performed a large genetic meta-analysis implicating Aβ, tau, immunity, and lipid processing in Alzheimer's risk (2,622 citations). (5) Games et al. (1995) reported Alzheimer-type neuropathology in transgenic mice overexpressing the V717F β-amyloid precursor protein (2,519 citations).
